source:
# PostScript grammar -- PARG source (parsanol grammar language).
# Normative source: the PostScript Language Guide
# (claricle/postscript-guide); each rule cites the guide page it
# derives from. Extraction target: the hand-written lexer/AST builder
# in claricle/postscript lib/postscript/source/ -- the rules below
# mirror that lexer's state machine (whitespace set, delimiter set,
# string escape set, DSC comments).
# Level 1/2/3 (per the design decision in claricle/postscript#4):
# this grammar is LEVEL-AGNOSTIC -- the operator vocabulary is registry
# metadata, not grammar structure. Level-gated literal forms (e.g.
# radix numbers, Level 2+) are marked inline.
# Compile: parsanol parg compile postscript.parg -o postscript.json

grammar PostScript version "0.1.0" {

  ## Program: any sequence of whitespace, comments, and objects.
  ## (guide: docs/syntax/tokens.adoc, docs/syntax/objects.adoc)
  program = 0*( ws / dsc_comment / comment / object )

  ## Whitespace: NUL HT LF FF CR SPACE (guide: docs/syntax/tokens.adoc).
  ws = 1*( %x00 / %x09 / %x0A / %x0C / %x0D / %x20 )

  ## Comment: "%" to end of line (guide: docs/syntax/tokens.adoc).
  comment = "%" 0*( !(%x0A / %x0D) ANY )

  ## DSC comment: "%%" line -- captured distinctly by the lexer
  ## (document structuring conventions; passes through to the model).
  dsc_comment = "%%" 0*( !(%x0A / %x0D) ANY )

  ## Objects (guide: docs/syntax/objects.adoc).
  ## Ordered choice: number/radix before name (a word is classified by
  ## shape, matching the lexer's scan_word_or_number + emit_word).
  object = radix / real / integer / string / hex_string / dictionary / array / procedure / literal_name / name

  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## Numbers (guide: docs/syntax/data-types.adoc)
  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------

  digit = %x30-39

  sign = ["+" / "-"]

  ## Integer: optional sign + digits. The !name_char guard enforces the
  ## lexer's maximal-munch word scan -- "123abc" is ONE name, not
  ## integer "123" + name "abc".
  integer = sign 1*digit !name_char

  ## Real: sign + (fraction and/or exponent) -- a bare digit run is an
  ## integer, so real requires "." or an exponent (e.g. 3.45, -7.89,
  ## 1.0e10, 6E23, -.002).
  real = sign ( 1*digit ["." 0*digit] exponent / 1*digit "." 0*digit / "." 1*digit [exponent] ) !name_char

  exponent = ( %x65 / %x45 ) [sign] 1*digit

  ## Radix number: base#value (e.g. 16#FF) -- LEVEL 2+ (marked per the
  ## level-gating decision; see claricle/postscript#4).
  radix = 1*digit "#" 1*( digit / %x41-5A / %x61-7A ) !name_char

  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## Strings (guide: docs/syntax/strings.adoc)
  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------

  ## Literal string: balanced parentheses, "\" escapes
  ## (\n \r \t \b \f \\ \( \), \ddd octal 1-3 digits, line continuations;
  ## unknown escapes stand for the escaped character -- mirrors
  ## lexer.rb handle_escape).
  string = "(" 0*( escaped / string / !(%x28 / %x29 / %x5C) ANY ) ")"
  escaped = "\\" ( 1*3(%x30-37) / ANY )

  ## Hex string: <hexdigits, whitespace allowed> (guide: docs/syntax/strings.adoc).
  hex_string = "<" 0*( hexdigit / ws ) ">"
  hexdigit = %x30-39 / %x41-46 / %x61-66

  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## Names (guide: docs/syntax/operators.adoc, docs/syntax/tokens.adoc)
  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------

  ## Delimiters: ( ) < > [ ] { } / %  -- terminate names.
  delimiter = %x28 / %x29 / %x3C / %x3E / %x5B / %x5D / %x7B / %x7D / %x2F / %x25

  ## Any byte that is neither a delimiter nor whitespace.
  name_char = !( delimiter / ws ) ANY

  ## Executable name: any run of non-delimiter, non-whitespace bytes.
  name = 1*name_char

  ## Literal name: "/" prefix (guide: docs/syntax/operators.adoc).
  literal_name = "/" name

  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## Composites
  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------

  ## Array: "[ objects ]" (guide: docs/syntax/arrays.adoc).
  array = "[" 0*( ws / comment / object ) "]"

  ## Procedure: "{ objects }" -- executable array; PEG recursion covers
  ## nesting (guide: docs/syntax/procedures.adoc).
  procedure = "{" 0*( ws / comment / object ) "}"

  ## Dictionary: "<< objects >>" (guide: docs/syntax/dictionaries.adoc).
  ## Keys and values are objects; pairing is semantic (the interpreter
  ## stack), not syntactic.
  dictionary = "<<" 0*( ws / comment / object ) ">>"

  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## Operator vocabulary
  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## Operators are executable names -- the vocabulary is REGISTRY
  ## metadata (Model::Operators), gated per Level 1/2/3 by profile
  ## validation after parsing (design decision: claricle/postscript#4).
  ## The guide's docs/commands/** categories enumerate the vocabulary.

  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------
  ## Smoke tests (full-input consumption enforced by the entry rule)
  ## ------------------------------------------------------------------
  entry main: program

  test main {
    accept "10 20 moveto (hi) show"
    accept "(nested (deep (deeper)) here) print"
    accept "/proc { 1 2 add } bind def"
    accept "[1 2 (three) /Four [5 6]] aload"
    accept "<</PageSize[612 792]>> setpagedevice"
    accept "<4f 4b> print"
    accept "16#FF setgray"
    accept "-.002 6.02E23 scale"
    accept "%%BeginSetup"
    accept "123abc print"
    reject "{ unclosed"
    reject "(unterminated"
    reject "<hex"
    reject "[1 2"
  }
}
